name: XENON
full_name: XENON experiment - neutrino and rare-decay programme
summary: The XENON series uses low-background liquid xenon primarily for dark-matter searches. Its neutrino programme includes solar-neutrino scattering and rare xenon decay processes, notably double-electron capture.
detection_principle: Prompt scintillation and delayed electroluminescence provide energy, position and interaction discrimination in a dual-phase TPC. Very low radioactive backgrounds allow rare electron-recoil and nuclear-recoil studies.

status.evidence: XENON1T observed the two-neutrino double-electron-capture decay of 124Xe, a rare standard weak process distinct from neutrinoless decay.

results.summary: XENON1T observed the two-neutrino double-electron-capture decay of 124Xe, a rare standard weak process distinct from neutrinoless decay.

XENONnT reported a low-energy solar-neutrino measurement using electron recoils. Its electron-scattering channel differs from coherent nuclear scattering; priority claims require comparison with earlier measurements.

science_scope: This is a multipurpose detector programme. Observed two-neutrino double-electron capture conserves lepton number and does not establish a Majorana neutrino mass.
